governanceNotes: D1 batch 31 (2026-09-23): deferred. Euthyroid sick syndrome (non-thyroidal illness syndrome) is an adaptive laboratory phenotype of severe systemic illness - low T3/T4 with nonspecific TSH changes occurring in critical illness, sepsis, starvation, and catabolic states - and is not an independent disease process (ME-41 manifestation-identity barrier, diplopia and encopresis precedents): any outcome edge would restate the severity of the underlying illness rather than an ESS-attributable effect. The literature direction is inverted (illness -> ESS), causation of downstream outcomes is confounded by the driving illness, and treating the laboratory changes has no established benefit. The thyroid identity targets (hypothyroidism, thyroiditis, thyroid-nodules) are true thyroid disease identities that ESS does not become.
Reopening condition: evidence that the ESS phenotype independently modifies outcomes after controlling for illness severity, with a catalog-fit target, would justify re-screening this identity.
